overview: Chipotle's Q2 revenue rose 9.3% to $3.3B on comparable sales of +2.2% (transactions +1%, pricing about 1.6%), with restaurant-level margin down 220 bps to 25.2% and adjusted EPS flat at $0.33. Adam Rymer, CFO, raised the full-year comp outlook to low single digits from about flat but guided Q3 to around +1% after comps softened about 200 bps in late July around an industry Cyclospora issue. Scott Boatwright, CEO, said Chipotle is not involved in that issue.
keyTakeaways: Adam Rymer, CFO, said traffic improved through Q2 and the first half of July before softening about 200 bps; the Q3 guide of around +1% assumes that headwind persists, implying roughly +3% underlying.

Scott Boatwright, CEO, said HEAP is in more than 1,000 restaurants, adding 2 to 3 entrees in the peak 15 minutes and 2 to 4 hours of daily labor efficiency, with 2,000 restaurants targeted by year-end.
Boatwright said 350 company-operated openings a year is the right pace, with incremental growth from Western Europe and partners; Alshaya already runs 15 restaurants.
Rymer said the pricing-inflation gap (about 1% versus low-to-mid 3% in the first half) narrows in Q3 and closes from Q4; Boatwright cited the highest wallet share gains since 2024.
financialHighlights: Revenue $3.3B, up 9.3%; comps +2.2% with transactions +1% and pricing about 1.6%; digital sales $1.3B, or 38.3% of sales versus 35.5%.
Restaurant-level margin 25.2%, down 220 bps: cost of sales 29.7% (+80 bps on beef and freight), labor 25% (+30 bps), other operating costs 14.9% (+90 bps), marketing 3%.
Adjusted diluted EPS $0.33, flat; non-GAAP G&A $176M; 101 openings including 80 Chipotlanes.
$631M repurchased at an average $32.55 (over $1.3B year to date), with $1.7B of authorization remaining; $800M of cash and no debt.
guidance: Adam Rymer, CFO, raised full-year comps to low single digits from about flat and guided Q3 comps to around +1%, assuming the roughly 200 bps Cyclospora-related softening continues against the toughest lap of the year.

Rymer expects Q3 pricing in the mid 2% range (full year near the high end of 1%-2%), cost of sales just under 30%, labor in the mid 25% range, other operating costs in the mid 15% range and marketing in the low 3% range.
Rymer guided Q3 non-GAAP G&A to around $180M, depreciation around 3% of sales and a 24%-26% tax rate, with pricing and inflation expected to match from Q4.

Scott Boatwright, CEO, expects approximately 350 openings in 2026 (about 80% Chipotlanes), HEAP in about 2,000 restaurants by year-end, a frictionless rewards pilot in August and a national catering launch in 2027.
risksMentioned: The industry Cyclospora issue cut comps about 200 bps in late July; Rymer called its duration "very difficult to predict".
Q3 is the toughest comparison of the year, per Rymer.
Beef and freight inflation and sequentially higher avocado prices, with first-half pricing of about 1% against inflation in the low-to-mid 3% range.
Investor pushback, raised by David Palmer of Evercore ISI, that heavy spending is yielding only 1%-2% comps.

qa.question: What is behind the low single-digit comp guide, the recent softening and the cadence from here?
qa.answer: Traffic improved through Q2 and the first half of July, then comps softened about 200 bps around the industry Cyclospora issue; Q3 is guided to around +1% assuming that continues. Scott Boatwright, CEO, said the implicated products are not on Chipotle's menu and its lettuce is sourced in California.

qa.question: Does the +1% Q3 guide with a 200 bps headwind imply about +3% underlying, and where is Max 15 throughput without HEAP?
qa.answer: Correct; the guide assumes the impact persists through the quarter. HEAP restaurants do two or three more entrees in Max 15; system in-store Max 15 is in the low 20s, digital adds mid-teens, for a combined low-to-mid 30s per restaurant per day.

qa.question: How does the margin outlook beyond Q3 look as the pricing-inflation gap narrows?
qa.answer: The gap was widest in the first half, with pricing around 1% and inflation in the low-to-mid 3% range; in Q3 inflation should be about 3% versus pricing in the mid 2% range, and from Q4 pricing and inflation are expected to match.

qa.question: Has Chipotle sized remodel capex and any sales uplift, and will it use partners in other international markets?
qa.answer: Chipotle has never done an aesthetic remodel; it is stage-gating a test at $100,000-$300,000 per restaurant across several geographies with nothing to report yet. Alshaya, Alsea and SPC operate as partners or JVs, while Chipotle owns Western Europe.
qa.read: Answered partially; no uplift or timeline.

unanswered.question: What is the LTO contribution to traffic uplift versus historical benchmarks?
unanswered.how: Adam Rymer, CFO, said no specific LTO lifts are disclosed, offering only that LTOs typically deliver hundreds of basis points.

unanswered.question: Is there an early read on remodel sales uplift and timeline?
unanswered.how: Scott Boatwright, CEO: "I have nothing to report today, unfortunately, but I'll tell you that work is in flight."

unanswered.question: What gives confidence that momentum picks up into 2027 given heavy spending for 1%-2% comps?
unanswered.how: Boatwright cited green shoots; the digital and brand plans were called industry changing but not shared.
